Alex / Procurement team,

Thanks for confirming the renewal window — we’re lining up our runbook now. I’ve attached a short manifest (soc2_evidence_manifest.xlsx) that lists the artifacts we’ll need to re-attest SOC 2: sample logs, configuration snapshots, access lists, and the last-year snapshot of our controls testing.

Quick asks to help us scope the work and any capacity impact:
- Can you confirm which log stores you expect us to export (application logs, API request logs, audit logs) and the retention window you want included in the attestation?
- Do you need a point-in-time export (single snapshot) or rolling slices (e.g., four weekly exports)?
- Will Helion provide a temporary S3 bucket for uploads, or should we push to a Redwood-provisioned bucket with limited retention?

Proposed timeline
- Jun 7: kickoff + manifest exchange (this message)
- Jun 10–12: Helion confirms scope + access
- Jun 15–18: evidence export run (we may request a short burst of dedicated capacity for faster extraction)
- Jun 25: internal verification + package handoff to your audit contact

We’ve flagged this for potential capacity scaling: depending on the log volume you confirm, we may propose a 48–72 hour burst on Dedicated to keep extraction within your window. I’ll loop in Karthik and Ben on the sizing once we have volumes.

Attachments: soc2_evidence_manifest.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks —

Hi Marissa — thanks for the manifest and timeline. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Scope: we need API request logs (90 days), authentication/audit logs (12 months), and a 30-day sample of application logs (we can point you to the index names).
2) Export type: single snapshot is OK for the audit binder, but the auditors asked for the option to re-run exports during the review, so rolling slices (weekly) would be ideal.
3) Upload: procurement will arrange a pre-provisioned S3 bucket (read/write for Redwood upload); I’ll share credentials via a secure link once procurement signs the amendment.

On capacity: our logs for the window are roughly 1.2 TB compressed for the 12-month audit window. If Redwood can provide an estimate for how long a bulk export would take on a default cluster vs. a 2-node Dedicated burst, that would help procurement with the amendment cost lines.

Procurement note: we’re aiming to finalize the amendment and signature by Jun 20.

— Alex

Marissa / Ben — scope and ask make sense. Estimated plan below: 

Summary estimates
- Baseline hosted export (no extra capacity): 1.2 TB compressed -> ~18–24 hours wall time using parallel export workers we run on hosted nodes (may push latency for other customers if run at full speed).
- 2-node Dedicated burst (48 hours): we can finish in ~3–5 hours wall time; 72 hours gives buffer for verification and re-runs.
- Rough cost delta to propose: $2,000–$3,500 for a 48-hour 2-node burst (depends on node type); we’ll firm after final node selection.

Security & runbook notes
- We will provide log-export-instructions.pdf with step-by-step export commands and a recommended verification checklist (checksums + sample record count).
- Use customer-provided S3 with an upload prefix limited by a short-lived IAM role we create; all uploads encrypted with Helion’s KMS key.
- Generate single-use presigned URLs for any manual uploads requested by auditors.

Operational plan
1) Jun 19: finalize index names and S3 details (Helion)
2) Jun 20: procurement signature; Redwood prepares IAM role and runs a dry-run on a 24-hour tiny sample
3) Jun 22–23: bulk export window on Dedicated burst (opt) or Jun 22: hosted export (if no burst requested)
4) Jun 24–25: verification and bundle handoff; provide redwood-soc2-summary-2025.pdf as part of the package

Attachments we’ll send to Helion: log-export-instructions.pdf, verification-checklist.txt (inline in runbook). I’ll prepare a short cost estimate doc for procurement after Marissa confirms we should propose the 48–72 hour burst.

If agreed, Ben, can you help draft the amendment cost lines and I’ll add the operational bullets to the statement of work?

Thanks —
